source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 23 iulie — «Sfinţii Mucenici Trofim şi Teofil»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Θεόφιλος, Τρόφιμος και άλλοι Δεκατρείς Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους». The Greek calendar keeps the company on 21 Ιουλίου and the Romanian row this folder already carries keeps it on 23 iulie: a different day on a different calendar, which is what the two rows are for, and the Greek listing for 23 Ιουλίου does not name them. The men are the folder's own: «Άγιοι Θεόφιλος, Τρόφιμος και άλλοι Δεκατρείς Μάρτυρες», thirteen companions counted and none named, in the reign of Diocletian, stoned, their flesh torn with iron instruments, their wounds burned with lighted tapers and at the last beheaded, which is the passion doxologia tells of «Sfinţii Mucenici Trofim şi Teofil». The Greek page gives the reign in years, «στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (284 - 304 μ.Χ.)», and that is taken into `dates`; the 304 is the page's own, where the reign is usually given as ending in 305. The thirteen are still named by nobody, so they get no folder, as the Romanian pass also left them. The same day's listing has «Άγιοι Ιούστος και Ματθαίος», whose page says they were martyred together with Theophilus and Trophimus; those two are drafted as new folders in this day's batch. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 05.08.2026 (23. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Трофим и Теофил, и још тринаест с њима.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4), and **it is an ENUMERATED COMPANY OF TWO WITH THIRTEEN MORE WHO ARE NOT ENUMERATED AT ALL** — «Трофим и Теофил, и још тринаест с њима». §5 counts the names the heading prints: two, and two folders are owed a row, both of which the corpus holds and which already relate one another. **The thirteen get nothing**, the heading naming not one of them and the body not returning to them — the same ruling that refused «и други с њим» on the Julian 2 August; the Greek line already on these folders counts them the same way, «και άλλοι Δεκατρείς Μάρτυρες». The quoted line is the one heading, whole, on both rows. **AND THE SERBIAN DAY IS THE ROMANIAN ONE AND NOT THE GREEK ONE, FOR THE SECOND TIME IN THREE DAYS.** Both folders are venerated romanian on **23/7** and venerated greek on **21/7**: saint.gr keeps the company two days earlier. This book prints them on the Julian 23 July, so both `serbian` rows are 23/7 and agree with the Romanian. No second-day note is owed by anybody; the two-day gap is the Greek calendar’s own and is recorded rather than reconciled. Ezekiel went the other way on the 21 July — Greek 23/7 against Romanian 21/7 — so the two calendars have now been found two days apart in both directions inside one week of this book. `types` UNTOUCHED. «Св.» is “saint” and «муч.» is the `martyr` both folders carry; the heading gives nothing else, and the tortures in the body are not ranks. **THE DATE, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST REFUSAL OF THIS RANGE BECAUSE THE YEAR IS OUTSIDE THE INTERVAL AND NOT INSIDE IT.** Both folders hold `death` earliest 284, latest 304, display «under Diocletian (284–304)», basis traditional, off saint.gr. This entry states a year outright: „Чесно пострадаше у Ликији 308. год.“ — they suffered honourably in Lycia **in the year 308**. **308 is not inside 284 to 304. It is four years after the end of it.** So this is not the narrowing rule’s case at all: a stated year fills an empty field and does not displace a recorded interval, and a year outside the interval would be a **widening**, which is the author’s and not a reader’s. Nothing is written, nothing is averaged, nothing is adjusted. **AND THE BOOK DOES NOT SIT WITH ITSELF, WHICH IS NOW A HABIT OF IT AND NOT AN ACCIDENT.** The same entry opens „Пострадаше у Ликији у време цара Диоклецијана.“ — they suffered in Lycia **in the time of the emperor Diocletian** — and Diocletian laid down the purple in 305, three years before the year the entry ends with. The corpus’s own interval IS that reign, as the Greek page gave it. So the book names the reign and then names a year outside it, exactly as the Julian 23 June named Valerian and then 275, and the Julian 22 June dated a council to 361 and put it under Jovian. **An emperor is no source for a year and a reign is not a date**, so neither statement is used to correct the other and both are recorded. The one-line alternative for the author is named in this batch’s commit message. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. „Пошто се никако не хтеше Христа одрећи, нити жртве идолима принети, то бише стављени на разне муке: тукоше их камењем, стругаше оштрим гвожђем, пребише им колена, и најзад тако измучене и више мртве него живе бацише их у огањ.“ — since they would in no way deny Christ nor sacrifice to the idols they were put to various torments: **beaten with stones, scraped with sharp iron, their knees broken**, and at the last, more dead than alive, thrown into the fire. „Сила Божја сачува их неповређене у огњу. Тада их изведоше и мачем посекоше.“, the power of God kept them unharmed in the fire, and then they were brought out and beheaded with the sword. „Но Господ их прослави и на земљи и у царству Свом небеском.“, the Lord glorified them both on earth and in his own heavenly kingdom. **The broken knees and the fire that would not burn them are in neither other book these folders hold.** NO NEW `related`: the two already relate each other both ways and the entry establishes nothing else. **The thirteen companions take no row because they take no folder**; the corpus holds `martyrs-slain-by-the-bulgars` and `seven-martyrs-at-carthage` on this same menologion number and neither is this company. No `office` on either. No `locations`: Lycia is named and is not written as a coordinate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr: «Οι άγιοι αυτοί, έζησαν στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (284 - 304 μ.Χ.)». The interval is that reign as the page prints it, which ends the reign in 304 where it is usually given as 305. The Romanian source the folder was built from named the reign and gave no years.

hymns.text: Яко воини, мученицы непобедимии,/ течением невозбранным в судилище неверных внидосте/ и веры ради многия муки претерпесте,/ Христа исповедающе Единаго со дерзновением./ Того молите, Трофиме и Феофиле с прочими,/ яко да тяготу страстей отложше,/ ваше ныне страдание поем, страстотерпцы непреоборимии.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 23 июля ст. ст. — «Тропарь мучеников Трофима, Феофила и с ними 13-ти мучеников», глас 4

english.text: As soldiers, O unconquerable martyrs, you went into the judgement hall of the unbelieving by a course nothing could bar, and for the faith's sake you endured many torments, confessing Christ alone with boldness. Entreat Him, O Trophimus and Theophilus with the rest, that laying aside the weight of the passions we may sing today of your suffering, O passion-bearers who cannot be overcome.

hymns.text: Мученицы Твои, Господи,/ во страданиих своих венцы пришла нетленныя от Тебе, Бога нашего:/ имуще бо крепость Твою,/ мучителей низложиша,/ сокрушиша и демонов немощныя дерзости./ Тех молитвами/ спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 23 июля ст. ст. — «Ин тропарь, общий, мучеников Трофима, Феофила и с ними 13-ти мучеников», глас 4; the page itself calls this one «общий», a common of martyrs, and it names no saint

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings have received incorruptible crowns from You, our God; for having Your strength, they cast down the tormentors and shattered also the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls.
